file: Apr 2026\N26173 - Training Sterility Samples Delayed and Missed Sterility Reads Scanning - USP 71 Signed by RS.pdf

description: On 16 Jan 2026, the training analyst AK performed USP <71> sterility test processing training in accordance with SOP 2.600.008 Rev. 18 (USP <71>/EP 2.6.1 Sterility Test). The supervised training activities were documented under submissions ETX‑260116‑0510, ETX‑260116‑0511, and ETX‑260116‑0513. The training covered the complete end‑to‑end sterility testing process, including sample preparation, testing, and relocation of samples to designated incubator rooms using handheld scanners. However, on the day of testing, preliminary data entry for the associated supervised samples was not performed. On 19 Jan 2026, the training analyst performed two unsupervised USP <71> sterility test trainings, documented under submissions ETX‑260116‑0514 and ETX‑260116‑0515. The testing activities were conducted in the same manner as the supervised training. For these unsupervised submissions, preliminary data entry was completed on the day of testing after the omission was noted by the supervisor. Review of the sterility test records determined that sterility reads for all submissions associated with the training analyst’s USP <71> sterility testing on 16 January 2026 and 19 January 2026 were not performed in accordance with the timing requirements specified in SOP 2.600.008 Rev. 18. For submissions ETX‑260116‑0510, ETX‑260116‑0511, and ETX‑260116‑0513, the last documented sterility read scans occurred on Day 49 of incubation. For submissions ETX‑260116‑0514 and ETX‑260116‑0515, no sterility read scans were documented in Eagle Trax sample scan history.
cause: Human Oversight - Inadvertent Extended delay and missed sterility scan reads
corrective_action: Test notes were added to appropriately document the missed sterility scan reads associated with the applicable training submissions. In response, all reading analysts and personnel involved in the affected trainings were required to complete a “read and understood” retraining for SOP #2.600.008, Revision 18, Section 8.4, with specific emphasis on ensuring that sterility scans are performed and completed in a timely manner. Sterility reading training was conducted separately, and the training analyst successfully performed the full sterility test process—excluding the scan sterility reads—in accordance with SOP #2.600.008, Revision 18 (USP <71> / EP 2.6.1 Sterility Test). Based on this assessment, there is minimal risk and no significant impact to the overall training qualification of the training analyst.

file: Apr 2026\N26218- Incubator Temperature went  out of specification  E001357 - USP 71 - MediaFill - Celsis - Signed by RS.pdf
equip_id: All samples listed in attached document
sample_id: All samples listed in attached document
lot_num: All samples listed in attached document
description: On 25 April 2027, at approximately 15:20 hours, a heater malfunction caused the temperature of walking incubator E001357 (specified range: 30–35 °C) to go out of specification. The temperature remained outside the specified range throughout 26 April 2026 and partially on 27 April 2026. Incubator E001357 is used for incubation of media bottles for sterility testing and samples for media fill testing. As a result of this unforeseen instrument malfunction, all samples incubated in E001357 during the affected period were potentially impacted.
cause: Incubator Heater Malfunction - Temperature out of specification.
corrective_action: Upon detection of the temperature excursion, the following corrective actions were implemented:The issue was immediately escalated to the Eagle Engineering team. An engineering analyst was assigned to this event to investigate the root cause and to expedite implementation of a permanent corrective solution for incubator E001357.As an interim corrective measure, multiple portable heaters were placed in the walk in incubator to restore and maintain the incubator temperature within the specified range. Temperature monitoring confirmed that the incubator returned to, and remained within, specification following implementation of this control.All media fill samples potentially impacted by this event will be over incubated by an additional 3 days. This extended incubation period ensures that the samples achieve sufficient incubation at the specified temperature conditions, thereby reducing the risk of false negative results. Celsis is a rapid microbial detection method that detects microbial growth through amplification of microbial ATP produced during microorganism replication. The amplified ATP is converted into a bioluminescent signal, allowing detection of microbial growth prior to the appearance of visual turbidity. The vendor established sensitivity for this technology is 5 days. Eagle has implemented a more conservative approach and routinely incubates sterility test samples analyzed by Celsis for 7 days. In addition, method suitability testing for Celsis requires confirmed growth of representative USP <71> organisms within 5 days. Furthermore, TSB media bottles incubated in incubator E001356 remained within temperature specification for the entire incubation period. Collectively, these factors support the conclusion that it is unlikely that this temperature excursion would result in false passing results for sterility testing performed using the Celsis method.All affected clients with sterility testing performed using USP <71> were notified by Client Care representatives. During these communications, the event and its potential impact were explained, and additional retest samples were requested for those samples that had completed Day 14 incubation prior to identification of the issue. It is important to note that samples that completed the sterility testing  after Day 14 incubation and before identification of the issue on 27 Apr 2026 were already read on the morning of 25 Apr 2025 at Day 12 of incubation. At that time, these samples showed no evidence of turbidity after 12 consecutive days of incubation at the appropriate temperature. Turbidity is a visual indicator that appears only after microbial growth reaches a threshold associated with exponential proliferation. It is therefore unlikely that exponential microbial growth would occur exclusively during the final one to two days of the sterility test. Furthermore, TSB media bottles incubated in incubator E001356 remained within temperature specification for the entire incubation period. Based on this scientific rationale, the likelihood of a false passing result is considered minimal. Nevertheless, Eagle has requested retesting out of an abundance of caution. The final decision regarding retesting ultimately rests with the client. For all USP <71> sterility tests that were not completed at the time of issue identification, the associated media bottles will be over incubated for an additional three (3) days to further reduce the potential for false negative or false passing results. The event, associated risks, and implemented corrective actions were reviewed with senior leadership to ensure appropriate oversight and to confirm that permanent corrective actions will be implemented for incubator E001357.

file: Aug 2026\N26389 - Missed verification for Scan RDI Sample - Scan RDI - Signed by QYC-RS.pdf
description: On 27Jul 26, the processing analyst PG completed the Scan RDI sterility process for the samples ETX-260723-0057, according to MICRO-SOP-12 for the ScanRDI sterility testing process. However, the sample was inadvertently not read and verified using the Scan RDI instrument by reading analysts on the first shift - PG, CSG, DT, and HS. This oversight appears to have been unintentional.
cause: Human Oversight - Inadvertent Missed Sterility Verification
corrective_action: The processing and reading analysts involved in this event were notified of the oversight and counseled on the importance of adherence to established sample handling, verification, and documentation procedures. Personnel were reminded to exercise increased diligence when performing sample processing, sample reading, and data transcription activities to minimize the risk of recurrence. As an immediate interim corrective action, first-shift personnel (PG, CSG, DT, and HS) will be required to complete documented "Read and Understood" training on MICRO-SOP-12 with specific emphasis on maintaining complete end-to-end chain of custody throughout the sample lifecycle, including sample receipt, preparation, processing, verification, result entry, and final disposition. Training will be issued via ZenQMS and documented. Due to the inability to verify the integrity and traceability of the affected sample result, the original sample will be invalidated and closed with a result designation of "-/-" to indicate an invalid result. A new submission ID will be generated, and testing will be repeated using additional sample vials, contingent upon sample availability. The Client Care team has been notified and will contact the client to request additional sample to support retesting activities as necessary. In addition, as of 03 Aug 2026, the Microbiology Laboratory Supervisor has implemented a mandatory worklist and checklist verification process for all processing and reading analysts. The worklist/checklist system will be utilized throughout each shift to provide documented accountability for sample receipt, processing, reading, verification and data entry, thereby ensuring all samples are appropriately tracked and accounted for prior to final reporting. This process is intended to strengthen sample traceability controls, improve workflow oversight, and reduce the likelihood of similar events occurring in the future.

description: On 05 Aug 2026, during Quality review of USP 71 Sterility samples, it was noted that there was a non-contemporaneous documentation discrepancy. The processing analysts ES and GS completed the USP <71> sterility testing procedure for the samples listed in the attached document, in accordance with MICRO-SOP-5 .  However, during routine sterility testing, analysts ES and GS inadvertently affixed incorrect sample identification labels to both the Fluid Thioglycollate Medium (FTM) and Tryptic Soy Broth (TSB) test bottles.  The labels applied reflected incorrect fraction numbers; consequently, the samples did not scan properly at the time of reading by analyst ANC, and this discrepancy prevented real-time data entry into the system.As a result, the test note documenting the discrepancy was not entered contemporaneously, but was instead recorded at the end of the 14-day incubation period, upon the final Day 14 sterility read, rather than at the time of occurrence.
cause: Incorrect mislabelling of BUD sample during USP <71> sterility testing setup.
corrective_action: As this mislabeling event was determined to be an isolated occurrence and not indicative of an adverse trend, the processing analysts were counseled on the requirements for accurate sample identification during USP <71> sterility test setup. Emphasis was placed on verifying BUD stability study sample identification labels prior to label application. The analysts were instructed to perform a thorough label verification of media bottles before test initiation to ensure accurate sample traceability and prevent the application of incorrect submission labels. Additionally, reading analysts were counseled on the requirement for contemporaneous documentation of testing discrepancies. the reading analysts were instructed to immediately document any observed sample identification, labeling, or data entry discrepancies through the use of test notes and to promptly notify supervisory personnel, as applicable, to ensure an accurate and complete record of event history.

file: Aug 2026\N26410 - Incorrect Use of Later Timepoint Label for BUD Multiple Samples - QYC - SIgned by DK-RS.pdf

sample_id: Multiple BUD Stability Study Samples for USP <71> sterility test

description: On 26Jun26 , 23 Jul 26 and 27Jul26, sterility testing analysts GS  (26 Jun 26 ) and AS (23 Jul 26 and 27 Jul 26) initiated sterility testing setup for samples associated with BUD stability studies in accordance with MICRO-SOP-5 (USP <71> / EP 2.6.1 Sterility Test). During labeling of the sterility media bottles, it was identified by Microbiology Lab supervisor that the analysts inadvertently generated and printed labels with incorrect fraction numbers for later time points instead of the required time points. The affected submissions were as follows:  ETX-260625-0235, for which T90 labels were printed instead of the required T0 labels on 26Jun26 by GS;ETX-260622-0620, for which T45 labels were printed instead of the required T30 labels on 23Jul26 by AS;ETX-260422-0459, for which T270 labels were printed instead of the required T90 labels on 23Jul26 by AS;ETX-250925-0273, for which T365 labels were printed instead of the required T300 labels on 23Jul26 by AS;ETX-260622-0618, for which T90 labels were printed instead of the required T30 labels on 23Jul26 by AS;ETX-260422-0457, for which T365 labels were printed instead of the required T90 labels on 23Jul26 by AS;ETX-260713-0600, for which T45 labels were printed instead of the required T0 labels on 27Jul26 by AS. A summary of the affected submissions and associated details is also provided in the attached table for reference. The analysts then proceeded to incubate the sterility tests using the incorrectly labeled time-point stickers, resulting in samples scheduled for the required time points being processed and incubated under incorrect later time-point designations.
cause: Inadvertent selection and verification of the incorrect time‑point fraction labels during USP <71> sterility test setup
corrective_action: Upon identification of the discrepancies, the incorrect sterility test labels associated with the affected BUD stability study submissions were removed and replaced with labels reflecting the required time points to ensure alignment with the approved BUD stability study testing schedules and sample identification requirements. Test notes were added to each affected sterility testing submission in EagleTrax to accurately document the event, including the original incorrect time-point designation, the corrective labeling performed, and the associated sterility test results, thereby maintaining traceability and preserving the testing history. As an interim measure, the Microbiology Laboratory Supervisor reviewed the events with analysts GS and AS and reinforced the requirement to verify the accuracy of stability study time-point labels prior to label printing, application, and test initiation. The analysts were instructed to exercise increased attention during sample setup activities involving stability study samples to prevent recurrence of similar labeling errors. Because similar errors occurred across multiple submissions and testing dates, the events were not considered isolated. Consequently, analysts will be required to perform a read and understood retraining on CORP-SOP-17 (Stability Studies) to get overview understanding of BUD stability studies and MICRO-SOP-5 (USP <71> / EP 2.6.1 Sterility Test) focusing section 8.4 for proper incubation of sample media bottles.

file: Aug 2026\N26421 - Damaged TSB Culture Media Bottle During Celsis Sterility Testing - QYC-RS.pdf
description: On 09Aug26, during routine sterility reads and Day 1 in-process checks in the TSB incubator room E001356, identified a strong odor and subsequently discovered a media spill within a sample incubation bin that set up by GL on 07 Aug 2026 Upon investigation, it was determined that the TSB culture media bottle associated with Celsis sterility test submission ETX-260805-0205 had been damaged and broken during incubation, resulting in loss of the culture media and inability to continue the original sterility test as intended according to MICRO-SOP-44 (Celsis Sterility Testing). The spilled media was promptly cleaned by EN, and the affected incubation bin, along with the remaining samples in the bin, was cleaned and disinfected. Additional inspection of all remaining incubation bins confirmed that no other samples were affected. Due to the damaged culture media bottle, the integrity of the original test could not be maintained and replacement sample vials were requested from the client to support repeat sterility testing under a new submission.
cause: Accidental breakage of the TSB culture media bottle
corrective_action: Immediately upon discovery, all spilled TSB media was cleaned, disinfected and removed from the incubator room. The affected incubation bin and all other samples contained within the bin were also cleaned and disinfected.  A comprehensive inspection of the remaining incubation bins was performed and no additional damaged samples were identified. The affected sterility test associated with ETX-260805-0205 will be invalidated due to loss of the original culture media bottle.  The Client Care team was notified and replacement sample vials were requested from the client. Additional sample was subsequently received under submission ID ETX-260810-0249 for repeat Celsis sterility testing.In addition, the Microbiology Laboratory Supervisor has reviewed the event with laboratory personnel and reinforced expectations regarding careful handling, storage, transport, and routine inspection of incubated sterility test samples. Personnel were reminded to maintain awareness of sample conditions during daily incubator checks and to immediately escalate any observed abnormalities. These actions are intended to strengthen sample handling controls and reduce the likelihood of similar events occurring in the future.
